question: The National Youth Policy was launched in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Youth Policy (NYP), 2014 was launched by the Government of India to replace the earlier National Youth Policy of 2003. (राष्ट्रीय युवा नीति — 2014)

 

• It defines "youth" as persons in the 15-29 years age group and lays down a vision to empower the youth to achieve their full potential and, through them, enable India to face global challenges.

 

• NYP 2014 identifies five clearly identifiable objectives and eleven priority areas, including education, employment and skill development, entrepreneurship, health, sports, and social values.

 

• It is administered by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, which also runs the National Youth Policy implementation through schemes like the National Service Scheme (NSS) and Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first National Youth Policy was formulated in 1988, followed by revisions in 2003 and then 2014.

 

• International Youth Day is observed every year on 12 August.

 

NOTE

 

• 2012 (Option 1): No National Youth Policy was launched in this year.

 

• 2013 (Option 2): No National Youth Policy was launched in this year.

 

• 2015 (Option 4): No National Youth Policy was launched in this year; NYP 2014 was already in force by then.

question: Which among the following was NOT a part of the three sections of the Rigvedic tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Craftsman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rigvedic tribe (jana) was broadly divided into three functional sections: the warriors/nobility (rajanya/kshatra), the priests (brahma), and the ordinary people/commoners (vish). (ऋग्वैदिक जनजाति — तीन वर्ग)

 

• The Rajan (chief/king) led the tribe in war and was assisted by tribal assemblies such as the Sabha and Samiti.

 

• Priests (Purohitas) performed sacrifices and rituals and advised the king, while the Vish (ordinary people/commoners) — cattle-rearers and cultivators — formed the bulk of the tribe.

 

• A distinct class of artisans/craftsmen (e.g., carpenters, smiths) did exist in Rigvedic society, but they were not one of the three broad tribal divisions described above; a formal, rigid varna-based occupational classification including craftsmen/Shudras emerged more clearly only in the Later Vedic period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The fourfold varna system (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) is first explicitly mentioned in the Purusha Sukta of the Rigveda (10th Mandala), a later addition to the text.

 

• The Sabha and Samiti were important tribal assemblies of the Rigvedic period that checked the powers of the king.

 

NOTE

 

• Priests (Option 2): They formed one of the three sections of the Rigvedic tribe.

 

• Ordinary people (Option 3): The Vish (commoners) formed one of the three sections of the Rigvedic tribe.

 

• Warriors (Option 4): The Rajanya/Kshatra (warrior nobility) formed one of the three sections of the Rigvedic tribe.

question: Who holds the record for the longest long jump in India as of 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jeswin aldrin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jeswin Aldrin set the current Indian national record in the men's long jump with a leap of 8.42 metres at the Indian Open Jumps Competition held in Thrissur, Kerala, in March 2023. (लंबी कूद राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्ड — जेस्विन एल्ड्रिन)

 

• His jump broke the previous long-standing national record of 8.30 m set by Suresh Babu in 2016, and improved on Murali Sreeshankar's 8.36 m mark from 2022.

 

• Jeswin Aldrin hails from Tamil Nadu and has represented India at the World Athletics Championships and other international meets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• T.C. Yohannan held the men's long jump national record (8.07 m) for nearly two decades from 1973 before it was broken.

 

• Murali Sreeshankar is a leading Indian long jumper who won a silver medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and gold at the 2023 Asian Athletics Championships.

 

NOTE

 

• TC Yohannan (Option 2): He was a former national record holder in men's long jump, but his record has since been surpassed.

 

• Murali S (Option 3): Murali Sreeshankar held the national record briefly before Jeswin Aldrin broke it in 2023.

 

• Nayana James (Option 4): She is a prominent Indian female long jumper, not the holder of the (men's) national long jump record referred to here.

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IX.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IX of the Indian Constitution, titled "The Panchayats", deals with the establishment and functioning of Panchayati Raj institutions. (पंचायत — भाग IX)

 

• It was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, and comprises Articles 243 to 243-O.

 

• This part provides for a three-tier Panchayati Raj system (Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad), direct elections, reservation of seats for SCs/STs/women, and the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission.

 

• The Eleventh Schedule, also added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects under the purview of Panchayats.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 simultaneously added Part IXA ("The Municipalities") dealing with urban local bodies, along with the Twelfth Schedule.

 

• The Panchayati Raj system was first recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957).

 

NOTE

 

• Part IV (Option 1): Deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

• Part VII (Option 3): Originally dealt with States in Part B of the First Schedule; it was repealed by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956.

 

• Part X (Option 4): Deals with the Scheduled and Tribal Areas.

question: Which of the following battles was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga in 1527?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Khanwa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 17 March 1527 near the village of Khanwa (present-day Rajasthan) between Babur and a confederacy of Rajput rulers led by Rana Sanga of Mewar. (खानवा का युद्ध — बाबर व राणा सांगा)

 

• Babur emerged victorious, which consolidated Mughal power in North India after his earlier victory over Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

 

• After the battle, Babur assumed the title of "Ghazi" (holy warrior) for defeating a large Rajput/"infidel" coalition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Chanderi (1528) was fought between Babur and Medini Rai, a former general of Rana Sanga, resulting in a Mughal victory.

 

• The Battle of Bayana (1527), a precursor skirmish before Khanwa, was actually won by Rana Sanga's forces against the Mughals.

 

NOTE

 

• Battle of Bayana (Option 1): This was a smaller preliminary engagement in February 1527 won by Rana Sanga, not the main 1527 battle against Babur.

 

• Second battle of Panipat (Option 3): This was fought in 1556 between Akbar and Hemu, not between Babur and Rana Sanga.

 

• Battle of Chanderi (Option 4): This was fought in 1528 between Babur and Medini Rai, not Rana Sanga.

question: Who among the following was the President of the Belgaum Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1924?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Belgaum Session of the Indian National Congress (December 1924) was presided over by Mahatma Gandhi. (बेलगाम अधिवेशन 1924 — महात्मा गांधी)

 

• This was the only time Gandhi ever presided over an annual session of the Indian National Congress.

 

• The session was significant for discussions on the Non-Cooperation Movement's aftermath, Hindu-Muslim unity, and the promotion of khadi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's presidency of the Belgaum session came in the aftermath of the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement (1922) following the Chauri Chaura incident.

 

• C.R. Das was the Congress president at the preceding Gaya Session (1922), where the Swaraj Party was formed by Das and Motilal Nehru.

 

NOTE

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 2): He presided over the Karachi Session, 1931, not the Belgaum session.

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 3): He presided over the Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939) sessions, not the Belgaum session.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 4): He presided over the Lahore Session, 1929 (where Purna Swaraj was declared), not the Belgaum session.

question: 'Atla Taddi' is the widely celebrated festival of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Atla Taddi (Atla Tadde) is a traditional festival widely celebrated by married and unmarried Telugu women, primarily in Andhra Pradesh (and also Telangana). (अట్ల తద్ది — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• It is observed on the third day (Tadiya/Tritiya) of the Krishna Paksha in the Hindu month of Ashvin, generally in September-October.

 

• Women observe a day-long fast (similar in spirit to Karva Chauth) and worship Goddess Gowri (Parvati), praying for the well-being and long life of their husbands/future husbands.

 

• The festival concludes the next morning with the preparation of "Atlu" (a type of rice pancake/dosa), from which the festival gets its name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atla Taddi is similar in theme to other regional festivals like Karva Chauth (North India) and Teej, all centred on fasting by women for marital well-being.

 

• Other important Telugu festivals include Bathukamma and Ugadi.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Its major festivals include Durga Puja and Poila Boishakh, not Atla Taddi.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Its major festivals include Baisakhi and Lohri, not Atla Taddi.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Its major festivals include Chhath Puja, not Atla Taddi.

question: Where was the 1st World Cup of Kabaddi organised in 2004?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Kabaddi World Cup, organised by the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF) (standard style), was held in Mumbai, India, in November 2004. (कबड्डी विश्व कप 2004 — मुंबई)

 

• The Indian team won this inaugural edition, defeating Iran in the final.

 

• This tournament, in the international/standard style of kabaddi, is distinct from the later Circle Style Kabaddi World Cups first held in Punjab in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has won every edition of the (standard style) Kabaddi World Cup it has participated in, underlining its dominance in the sport.

 

• Kabaddi is also part of the Asian Games, where India has historically been the dominant team as well.

 

NOTE

 

• Hyderabad (Option 2): This was not the host city of the 1st Kabaddi World Cup in 2004.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Punjab hosted the first Circle Style Kabaddi World Cup in 2010, not the 2004 standard-style World Cup.

 

• Kolkata (Option 4): This was not the host city of the 1st Kabaddi World Cup in 2004.

question: In which of the following states of India is Hojagiri dance predominantly performed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hojagiri dance is a traditional folk dance of the Reang (Bru) tribe of Tripura, performed during the Hojagiri festival dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi. (होजागिरी नृत्य — त्रिपुरा)

 

• It is performed exclusively by young girls and women who balance on top of an earthen pitcher (ghara) while simultaneously balancing objects like a bottle on the head and an earthen lamp in the hand, without any instrumental accompaniment — the rhythm is provided by their own singing.

 

• The dance showcases remarkable physical balance and is one of the most distinctive tribal dance forms of Northeast India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important tribal dances of Tripura include Garia and Lebang Boomani.

 

• Tripura's Hojagiri dance is often showcased at national cultural festivals, including the Republic Day parade.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Its notable dance forms include Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, not Hojagiri.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Its notable dance forms include Nati, not Hojagiri.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Its notable dance forms include Lavani, not Hojagiri.

question: Which of the following is related to neem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pinnately.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The neem tree (Azadirachta indica) has pinnately compound leaves, where multiple leaflets are arranged on either side of a common central axis (rachis), like a feather. (नीम — पिच्छाकार पत्तियाँ)

 

• Pinnate leaf venation/arrangement is common among many trees such as neem, rose, and tamarind, distinguishing them from plants with simple or palmately compound leaves.

 

• Neem is widely valued in India for its medicinal, antibacterial, and pesticidal properties, and its leaves, bark, seeds and oil are used extensively in Ayurveda and organic farming.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Palmately compound leaves, where leaflets radiate from a single point (like fingers from a palm), are seen in plants such as the silk cotton tree and Bombax.

 

• Tendrils (as in grapevine, pea) and spines (as in cactus, Opuntia) are examples of leaf modifications, unrelated to neem's leaf structure.

 

NOTE

 

• Tendril (Option 1): Tendrils are thread-like modified leaves/stems used for climbing, as seen in pea and grapevine, not neem.

 

• Palmately (Option 2): Palmately compound/veined leaves are seen in plants like papaya and silk cotton tree, not neem.

 

• Spines (Option 4): Spines are modified leaves seen in xerophytic plants like cactus, not neem.

question: What is the position of India in the world's telecommunication market, as of March 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India is the world's second-largest telecommunication market, after China, in terms of the number of subscribers/connections. (दूरसंचार बाजार — दूसरा स्थान)

 

• As per TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India) data, India had over 1.19 billion telecom subscribers as of early 2024, with a growing share of 5G connections.

 

• India is also the world's largest data-consuming nation per subscriber, driven by affordable data tariffs following the entry of Reliance Jio in 2016.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India rolled out 5G services commercially starting October 2022, and had achieved rapid pan-India 5G coverage by 2024.

 

• TRAI is the regulatory body governing the telecommunications sector in India, established in 1997.

 

NOTE

 

• Fourth (Option 1): India ranks higher than fourth in the world telecom market by subscriber base.

 

• Third (Option 2): India ranks higher than third in the world telecom market by subscriber base.

 

• First (Option 3): China, not India, is the largest telecommunication market in the world by subscriber base.

question: Which national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is home to species like Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Campbell Bay National Park.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Campbell Bay National Park, located on Great Nicobar Island, is home to species such as the Nicobar Megapode, crab-eating (long-tailed) Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and the Giant Robber Crab (Coconut Crab). (कैंपबेल बे राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — ग्रेट निकोबार द्वीप)

 

• It was established in 1992 and forms part of the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve, one of India's biodiversity hotspots.

 

• The park harbours unique flora and fauna found only in this region, including several endemic and endangered species.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important protected areas in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands include the Mount Harriet National Park, Saddle Peak National Park, and Rani Jhansi Marine National Park.

 

• The Great Nicobar Island is also known for the Shompen and Nicobarese tribal communities.

 

NOTE

 

• Raimona National Park (Option 1): This is located in Assam, not the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

• Mouling National Park (Option 3): This is located in Arunachal Pradesh, not the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

 

• Papikonda National Park (Option 4): This is located in Andhra Pradesh, not the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

question: A chemical reaction in which the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the first power of the concentration of the reacting substance is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is first order reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A first order reaction is one in which the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the first power (concentration^1) of a single reactant's concentration, i.e., Rate = k[A]^1. (प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया — First Order Reaction)

 

• Its integrated rate equation is k = (2.303/t) log([A]₀/[A]), and its half-life is independent of the initial concentration.

 

• Common examples of first order reactions include radioactive decay and the decomposition of N₂O₅.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a zero order reaction, the rate is independent of the concentration of reactants (Rate = k).

 

• The order of a reaction is determined experimentally and can be a whole number, fraction, or zero, unlike molecularity which is always a whole number.

 

NOTE

 

• Zero order reaction (Option 1): Here the rate does not depend on the concentration of the reactant at all (Rate = k[A]⁰).

 

• Third order reaction (Option 2): Here the rate depends on the cube of concentration terms (sum of powers = 3), not the first power.

 

• Second order reaction (Option 3): Here the rate depends on the square of concentration terms (sum of powers = 2), not the first power.

question: For which film did Asha Bhosle win the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award in the Best Playback Singer Female category in 2002?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lagaan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asha Bhosle won the IIFA Award for Best Female Playback Singer at the 3rd IIFA Awards (2002) for the song "Radha Kaise Na Jale" from the film Lagaan (2001). (लगान — आशा भोसले, आईफा पुरस्कार 2002)

 

• Lagaan, directed by Ashutosh Gowariker and starring Aamir Khan, was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2002.

 

• The music of Lagaan was composed by A.R. Rahman, and the film's soundtrack remains one of the most celebrated in Hindi cinema.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asha Bhosle is one of the most prolific playback singers in the world, known for her versatility across genres, and is the recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2000).

 

• The IIFA Awards were established in 2000 and are known for holding their annual ceremony in a different international city each year.

 

NOTE

 

• Devdas (Option 1): This 2002 film starred Shah Rukh Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and is unrelated to Asha Bhosle's 2002 IIFA win.

 

• Humraz (Option 2): This is not the film for which Asha Bhosle won this particular IIFA award.

 

• Om Jai Jagdish (Option 3): This is not the film for which Asha Bhosle won this particular IIFA award.

question: The government of which of the following states allocated ₹11,728 crore for the Aasara pension scheme in its annual budget for the fiscal year 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Telangana government allocated ₹11,728 crore for the Aasara pension scheme in its annual budget for the fiscal year 2022-23. (ఆసరా पेंशन योजना — तेलंगाना)

 

• The Aasara Pension Scheme provides monthly financial assistance to old-age persons, widows, persons with disabilities, weavers, toddy tappers, and persons with HIV/AIDS in Telangana.

 

• The scheme was launched in 2014 by the Telangana government soon after the state's formation, and pension amounts have been periodically enhanced.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Telangana's other major welfare schemes include Rythu Bandhu (farmer investment support) and Kalyana Lakshmi/Shaadi Mubarak (marriage assistance).

 

• Telangana was formed as India's 29th state on 2 June 2014, carved out of Andhra Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Odisha runs its own pension scheme called Madhu Babu Pension Yojana, not Aasara.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): This state did not allocate this particular sum for the Aasara pension scheme.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 4): This state did not allocate this particular sum for the Aasara pension scheme.

question: The Permanent Settlement came into operation in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1793.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 for the provinces of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. (स्थायी बंदोबस्त — 1793, लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस)

 

• Under this system, Zamindars were recognised as the permanent, hereditary owners of land, in exchange for paying a fixed annual revenue to the East India Company in perpetuity.

 

• The system was based on the recommendations of John Shore and James Grant, and was initially introduced on a ten-year (decennial) basis in 1790 before being made permanent in 1793.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major land revenue systems in British India included the Ryotwari System (introduced by Thomas Munro/Alexander Read in Madras and Bombay presidencies) and the Mahalwari System (introduced in parts of North India).

 

• Lord Cornwallis also reorganised the civil services and judiciary in British India during his tenure as Governor-General.

 

NOTE

 

• 1890 (Option 1): This is not the year of the Permanent Settlement.

 

• 1790 (Option 2): This was when the settlement was introduced on a decennial (ten-year) basis, before being made permanent in 1793.

 

• 1789 (Option 3): This is not the year of the Permanent Settlement.

question:
Consider the following statements related to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) handbook.

1.It will be launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology.

2.ODR is the resolution for cases outside courts using digital technology and techniques of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), such as negotiation, mediation and arbitration.

3.The development of ICT and increased use of internet has played a major role for ODR.

Which of the given statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Handbook was launched by NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of Science and Technology, making Statement 1 incorrect. (ऑनलाइन विवाद समाधान — नीति आयोग)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: ODR refers to resolving disputes outside traditional courts using digital technology, combined with Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) techniques like negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The growth of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and rising internet penetration have been major enabling factors for the adoption of ODR in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ODR Handbook was released in 2021 as part of NITI Aayog's efforts to make justice more accessible, timely, and affordable.

 

• The push for ODR gained momentum especially after the COVID-19 pandemic, which necessitated remote and digital resolution of disputes.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 1): This is incorrect because it includes the false Statement 1.

 

• Only 1 (Option 3): This is incorrect as Statement 1 itself is false.

 

• Only 2 (Option 4): This is incomplete as it excludes the correct Statement 3.

question: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian constitution?
option_1: India that is Bharat as federation of states
option_2: India that is Bharat as parliamentary democracy
option_3: India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states
option_4: India that is Bharat as presidential form of democracy
solution_text:
The correct answer is India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 1 of the Indian Constitution states: "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States." (संघ राज्य — अनुच्छेद 1)

 

• The term "Union of States" was deliberately preferred by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar over "Federation of States" to indicate that Indian federalism is not the result of an agreement among states, and that no state has the right to secede from the Union.

 

• Article 1 also states that India shall consist of the territories of the states, Union Territories, and any other territories that may be acquired.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 1 falls under Part I of the Constitution, titled "The Union and its Territory," covering Articles 1 to 4.

 

• Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing states by a simple majority.

 

NOTE

 

• India that is Bharat as federation of states (Option 1): Article 1 explicitly uses "Union of States," not "federation of states."

 

• India that is Bharat as parliamentary democracy (Option 2): The parliamentary form of government is described elsewhere (e.g., Article 74, 75), not in Article 1.

 

• India that is Bharat as presidential form of democracy (Option 4): India does not follow a presidential system, and this is not mentioned in Article 1.

question: The Flexible Inflation Targeting Framework (FITF) was introduced in India post the amendment of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934 in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Flexible Inflation Targeting Framework (FITF) was formally introduced in India through an amendment to the RBI Act, 1934, in 2016. (लचीली मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्यीकरण ढांचा — 2016)

 

• As part of this framework, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body, was constituted to determine the policy repo rate needed to keep inflation within the target set by the government.

 

• The inflation target was set at 4% (Consumer Price Index), with a tolerance band of +/- 2%, to be reviewed every five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) comprises three members from the RBI (including the Governor as Chairperson) and three external members appointed by the Government of India.

 

• The inflation targeting framework was first recommended by the Urjit Patel Committee (2014).

 

NOTE

 

• 2014 (Option 1): This is the year the Urjit Patel Committee recommended inflation targeting, not the year FITF was formally introduced via the amendment.

 

• 2010 (Option 2): FITF was not introduced in this year.

 

• 2020 (Option 4): FITF was not introduced in this year; the framework was already in operation and up for its first review around this time.

question: What is the duration of monsoon in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100-120 days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Southwest Monsoon season in India typically lasts about 100-120 days, from June to September. (भारतीय मानसून अवधि — 100-120 दिन)

 

• The monsoon usually arrives at the Kerala coast around 1 June and progressively covers the entire country by mid-July, before withdrawing from Rajasthan by around mid-September.

 

• India receives about 75% of its annual rainfall during this four-month monsoon period, making it crucial for agriculture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's monsoon system is broadly divided into the Southwest Monsoon (June-September) and the Northeast/Retreating Monsoon (October-December), the latter bringing rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu.

 

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is responsible for monsoon forecasting in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• 40-60 days (Option 2): This underestimates the actual duration of the Indian monsoon season.

 

• 150-200 days (Option 3): This overestimates the actual duration of the Indian monsoon season.

 

• 50-80 days (Option 4): This underestimates the actual duration of the Indian monsoon season.

question: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Executive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part V of the Indian Constitution, titled "The Union," covers Articles 52 to 151, and its first chapter (Articles 52 to 78) deals specifically with the Union Executive. (संघीय कार्यपालिका — भाग V)

 

• This chapter covers the President (Art. 52-62), Vice-President (Art. 63-71), Council of Ministers and Prime Minister (Art. 74-75), Attorney General of India (Art. 76), and Conduct of Government Business (Art. 77-78).

 

• Article 74 provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later chapters of Part V deal with Parliament (Art. 79-122), Legislative Powers of the President (Art. 123), and the Union Judiciary (Art. 124-147), among others.

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is dealt with under Article 148, also within Part V.

 

NOTE

 

• Finance Commission of India (Option 1): This is dealt with under Article 280, in Part XII of the Constitution.

 

• Amendment of the Constitution (Option 3): This is dealt with under Article 368, in Part XX.

 

• National emergency (Option 4): This is dealt with under Article 352, in Part XVIII.

question: Ali Akbar Khan is known for playing the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan was a legendary Indian classical musician renowned for playing the Sarod. (सरोद — अली अकबर खान)

 

• He was the son and disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan of the Maihar gharana, and was popularly known as "Khansahib" or "Ustad ji."

 

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna-adjacent civilian honours, including the Padma Vibhushan (1989), and received multiple Grammy Award nominations for his contributions to Indian classical music globally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other renowned Sarod maestros include Amjad Ali Khan and Buddhadev Dasgupta.

 

• Ali Akbar Khan founded the Ali Akbar College of Music in Kolkata (1956) and later in San Rafael, California (1967), to promote Indian classical music worldwide.

 

NOTE

 

• Ektara (Option 1): This is a one-stringed instrument commonly used by Baul singers and folk performers, not associated with Ali Akbar Khan.

 

• Sarangi (Option 2): This bowed string instrument is famously associated with maestros like Ustad Sultan Khan, not Ali Akbar Khan.

 

• Tanpura (Option 3): This is a drone instrument used to accompany vocal or instrumental performances, not Ali Akbar Khan's primary instrument.

question: The northern plain of the Indian subcontinent has been formed by the interplay of the three major river systems along with their tributaries. Choose the odd one out of the options given.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Godavari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Northern Plains of India have been formed primarily by the alluvial deposition of three major Himalayan river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra, along with their tributaries. (उत्तरी मैदान — सिंधु, गंगा, ब्रह्मपुत्र)

 

• These are all perennial, glacier/snow-fed rivers originating in the Himalayas, carrying large volumes of silt that have built up the fertile alluvial plains over millions of years.

 

• The Godavari, in contrast, is a Peninsular (South Indian) river, rain-fed, and originates from the Western Ghats (Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra) — it plays no role in forming the Northern Plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Godavari is the largest Peninsular river in India and is often called the "Dakshin Ganga" (Ganga of the South).

 

• The Northern Plains are conventionally divided into the Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, and Khadar regions based on the nature of alluvial deposits.

 

NOTE

 

• The Brahmaputra (Option 1): This is one of the three Himalayan rivers that formed the Northern Plains.

 

• The Indus (Option 2): This is one of the three Himalayan rivers that formed the Northern Plains.

 

• The Ganga (Option 3): This is one of the three Himalayan rivers that formed the Northern Plains.

question: Name the phenomenon where an opaque object on the path of light becomes very small and where light has a tendency to bend around it and not walk in a straight line.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diffraction of light.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Diffraction of light is the phenomenon in which light bends around the edges of a small obstacle or aperture (of size comparable to its wavelength) instead of travelling strictly in a straight line. (प्रकाश का विवर्तन — Diffraction)

 

• It occurs prominently when the size of the obstacle or slit is very small, close to the wavelength of the light wave, causing the wave to spread into the region of the geometrical shadow.

 

• Diffraction is strong evidence for the wave nature of light, and is responsible for effects like the colourful patterns seen on a CD/DVD surface and the spreading of light through a narrow slit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diffraction should not be confused with refraction (bending of light while passing from one medium to another) or reflection (bouncing back of light from a surface).

 

• The phenomenon of diffraction was famously demonstrated through Young's Double Slit Experiment, which also confirmed the wave nature of light.

 

NOTE

 

• Reflection of light (Option 1): This refers to light bouncing back from a surface, not bending around small obstacles.

 

• Angle of refraction (Option 3): This is the angle made by a refracted ray with the normal when light passes between two media of different densities, unrelated to bending around small obstacles.

 

• Angle of incidence (Option 4): This is the angle at which an incident ray strikes a surface, unrelated to the bending phenomenon described.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

i. The first green revolution led to over-exploitation of natural resources.

ii. The second Green Revolution was more focused on Southern India.

iii. The second green revolution ensured in achieving sustainable livelihood security.
solution_text:
The correct answer is i and iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement i is correct: The First Green Revolution (led by M.S. Swaminathan in the 1960s-70s) significantly boosted foodgrain production but also led to over-exploitation of natural resources — including groundwater depletion, soil degradation, and excessive fertiliser/pesticide use. (हरित क्रांति — प्राकृतिक संसाधनों का अति-दोहन)

 

• Statement iii is correct: The Second Green Revolution (Evergreen Revolution), also championed by M.S. Swaminathan, aimed at increasing productivity in perpetuity without ecological harm, thereby helping achieve sustainable livelihood security for farmers.

 

• Statement ii is incorrect: The Second Green Revolution/"Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)" initiative was focused primarily on the Eastern states — Bihar, Eastern Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Odisha, Assam, and Chhattisgarh — not Southern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Green Revolution was concentrated mainly in Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh, centred on high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice.

 

• M.S. Swaminathan, known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India," was awarded the first World Food Prize (1987) and the Bharat Ratna (2024, posthumously).

 

NOTE

 

• Only ii (Option 2): This is incorrect since Statement ii itself is factually wrong.

 

• ii and iii (Option 3): This is incorrect because it includes the false Statement ii.

 

• i and ii (Option 4): This is incorrect because it includes the false Statement ii and excludes the correct Statement iii.
